steps.title: 01-signin: Sign in to Grafana with username admin and password admin. If a 'Welcome to Grafana' or 'Update your password' prompt appears, skip it. Then navigate to Dashboards, find the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health', open it, and report the titles of all panels on that dashboard exactly as shown on screen.

02-create: Create a NEW dashboard in Grafana. Add a new visualization panel, set its visualization type to 'Stat', set the panel title to exactly '{{runid}} Availability', and set its query data source to the TestData data source (it may be named 'TestData DB' or similar - pick the test data source, not the default). Then save the dashboard with the title exactly '{{runid}} {{01-signin.dashboard_folder}} Dashboard' (use Save dashboard, enter the title, confirm Save). Verify the save succeeded (no unsaved-changes indicator), then report the browser's current page URL and the panel title as shown on the dashboard.

03-open: On the currently open dashboard '{{runid}} {{01-signin.dashboard_folder}} Dashboard' (URL http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard), enter edit mode and add a NEW Text panel. Set the Text panel's title to exactly '{{runid}} Notes' and set its text content to include the string '{{runid}}' (e.g. write something like '{{01-signin.dashboard_folder}} notes for run {{runid}} - created by automation.'). Then save the dashboard (Save dashboard, confirm Save) and verify the save succeeded with the 'Dashboard saved' alert and no unsaved-changes indicator. Exit edit mode without any discard prompt. Report the panel titles now visible on the dashboard and the text content shown in the Notes panel.

04-open: On the currently open dashboard '{{runid}} {{01-signin.dashboard_folder}} Dashboard' (URL http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard), do two things and save: (1) Open Dashboard settings (gear/cog icon) and add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard's tags (in the Settings > General section, Tags field, type 'bench' and press Enter so it becomes a tag chip), then save/apply the settings. (2) Back on the dashboard, use the time range picker in the top bar to set the time range to 'Last 6 hours'. Then open Save dashboard and MAKE SURE the 'Update default time range' checkbox is TICKED before clicking Save, so the 6-hour range is persisted into the saved dashboard. Verify the 'Dashboard saved' alert appears and there are no unsaved changes (exiting edit mode or reloading should not prompt to discard). Report: the tags shown in dashboard settings, the time range shown in the top bar, and whether the 'Update default time range' box was ticked when you saved.

05-open: On the currently open dashboard '{{runid}} {{01-signin.dashboard_folder}} Dashboard' (URL http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard), set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m'. Do this via Dashboard settings (gear icon) → General → 'Auto refresh' / 'Refresh every' dropdown, selecting '1m' (1 minute). Then save the dashboard settings and save the dashboard so the change persists (verify with the 'Dashboard saved' alert and no unsaved-changes indicator; exiting edit mode should not prompt to discard). Then do a full page reload and re-open Dashboard settings to verify the Auto refresh value still reads '1m'. Report the auto-refresh value you observed in settings after the reload, and the browser's current page URL.

06-open: Final verification of the dashboard '{{runid}} {{01-signin.dashboard_folder}} Dashboard'. Open a fresh browser load of http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard (no extra query params) and confirm all of the following from the live page, reporting each: (a) the dashboard title shown in the breadcrumb/page, (b) the titles of every panel on the dashboard, (c) the time range shown in the top bar time picker, (d) the refresh interval shown in the top bar refresh picker, (e) the tag 'bench' visible on the dashboard (e.g. in the dashboard header/toolbar or via Dashboard settings > General tags), and (f) open the panel editor for the panel titled '{{runid}} Availability' and confirm its visualization type is 'Stat' and its query data source is the TestData data source, then exit edit mode WITHOUT saving (discard if prompted, since you changed nothing). Finally report the browser's exact current page URL.
